results.title: Poddle: Swing your phone, play pickleball on any computer! | Product Hunt
results.content:
To move around the court, your webcam tracks where you stand. The video never leaves your computer. No camera? The game runs you to the ball automatically, like Wii Sports tennis, so you just swing.  
  
Early into the project, I added phone support for ease of testing. It ended up staying, though, since everyone already has one, and the time to play was so much faster than AirPods.  
  
You can also play Matt the bot at various difficulties, play friends online, earn trophies, run a knockout tournament, or watch live matches.  
  
Poddle is free, and you don't need an account unless you’re someone who likes progression and tracking your stats. Any feedback on how the swing feels and on potential future features is greatly appreciated. Have fun! 🥒 [...] ### Top forum threads

What do you think? …

Daniel

Hey Product Hunt, I'm Daniel, and this is my first launch! 😁  
  
Poddle started as a last-minute hackathon idea. AirPods have motion sensors, so we wondered if one could work as a pickleball paddle, in Wii Sports fashion. And it worked better than we expected! We didn't win anything, but I kept building it anyway out of love for the idea of the project, and I've been having tons of fun with my friends at university clubs playing and testing it ever since.  
  
Most of my time went into making the swing feel right. A motion sensor knows how your hand turns, not where it is, so the game reads the swing itself: speed and reach set the power, direction aims it, a scoop lobs it, and a wrist cut adds spin. [...] Poddle

results.title: Superhuman Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
results.content:
#### What needs improvement

The AI writing is great for replies, but I'd love to see it get better at matching my tone for cold outreach. It sometimes feels a bit too formal for the kind of emails I send day to day.

#### vs Alternatives

Gmail

Gmail is where I started, and it works fine for basic stuff. But once your inbox gets busy with outreach and launch coordination, it just doesn't keep up. No smart sorting, no snippets, no AI assist. Superhuman felt like an actual upgrade, not just a different skin.

Michael D

#### What's great [...] #### What needs improvement

The biggest downside is the price and how techie it feels, many non-technical people say its not for them. It’s expensive compared with Gmail and Outlook, so you really need to use it heavily to justify the cost. It is more for people that value their precious minutes and hours saved by using the keyboard shortcuts and AI features.

I’d also like more flexibility around tagging and inbox organization. A few parts of the interface can feel a little restrictive once you have a more complex email workflow. The split inboxes work well but there could be more drag and drop functionality, more tagging options etc.

#### vs Alternatives

Gmail
NotionMail
Outlook for Mac

I’ve used Gmail and Outlook for years, and have also tried a few other email clients. [...] #### What's great

Superhuman is an excellent example of UX/UI geared to human use and efficiency. It's incredible how they've continued to develop improvements, and been able to maintain the mantra of making email EASY. The Splits are one of my favorite features, and the way they continue to integrate AI is sensible, effective, and NOT just to be able to say they've "got AI". Summaries, writing assistance, and able to do it in YOUR voice, is pretty remarkable. It's not perfect, but it's really close. Editing my email after asking for my voice takes moments instead of large re-writes. Keyboard shortcuts galore - thank goodness I don't have to go looking for my mouse to interact. Ctrl-K is something I want EVERY solution to implement. I continue to pay for this, and don't see that ending.
